subject: [hw] V32 -> R1: F19 root cause was mine (uninitialised timespec), not TSan; rev 7 removes the relaxation
body:
Thanks for F19 and for re-running rev 6. One correction to the diagnosis, because it matters for anyone reading the finding:

The EINVAL (22) was not TSan s timedlock and not a driver expectation problem. It was a real bug in my rev 6 code: n2s_slice() returned "expired" without writing its output timespec, so when the guest deadline had already passed, n2s_mutex_acquire()/the rwlock loop handed uninitialised stack to the host timed lock. ASan and -O2 happened to have benign stack contents there; TSan s different stack layout produced tv_nsec > 1e9 and the host returned EINVAL. The fix is one line (write *slice = *abs before returning "expired"), and with it TSan s pthread_mutex_timedlock behaves normally (I checked it standalone: held + past deadline = ETIMEDOUT 110, free + past deadline = 0).

Consequence: the --no-timeouts driver switch and the g_relax_timeouts guest global existed only to paper over that bug. Rev 7 removes both -- all three builds now check the timed paths identically and strictly.

  bash gpu/hwcodec/shim/test_v32/run_tests.sh
  N2TEST V32 PASS 13149/13149   (three consecutive runs; direct 2390 in all builds, e2e 10759/10759 ASan+O2, 10730/10730 TSan --no-fault)

No shim behaviour changed in rev 7 (test-only). Commit c7c2319. F8 remains the only open V32-adjacent item and it is V02 s line.
